newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end pre-holiday session steady.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end pre-holiday session steady.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended a shortened session little changed Tuesday, ahead of the Christmas holiday Wednesday.
Both COMEX and NYMEX precious metals trading will close for the Christmas holiday Wednesday and resume Thursday.
COMEX February gold closed unchanged at $370.60 an ounce, after trading in a narrow $370.80-370.30 range, on total estimated gold futures volume of only 5,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $368.60/369.10, against the London Tuesday morning fix at $368.90 and the New York close Monday at $368.60/369.10.
There was no London afternoon gold fix Tuesday and the next fix will be on Friday morning, after the Christmas and Boxing Day holiday in London.
March silver closed up 1.0 cent at $4.873 an ounce, after trading in a $4.875-4.855 range on total estimated silver volume of only 3,000 lots.

After seeing the year's lows in late November, the precious metals complex has ended the year on a quiet note, but sentiment remains slightly bearish going into 1997, with potential central bank selling still hanging over the market in the new year, analysts said.

"Upside price potential (for gold) remains capped by prospects for selling pressure from central banks and producers, coupled with weaker-than-anticipated demand in the physical markets," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
In the last few weeks, market rumors suggested a 10 million ounce central bank sale had been occurring, despite denials by the Dutch, Belgian and Portuguese central banks.

"The path of least resistance for gold prices is likely to remain to the downside unless bearish sentiment is dampened by significant price corrections in financial and/or foreign exchange markets," he said.
NYMEX April platinum ended down 50 cents at $376.40. NYMEX January platinum enters its delivery period January 1.
NYMEX March palladium closed up five cents at $$118.75.
